name: Enclosure
summary: An email composer whose paperclip pops up to stop you sending a message that mentions a missing file
about: A mail window that reads what you write. When the subject or body says attached, attachment or enclosed and nothing is attached, the words get a coral underline and Send is caught: the plane lunges, a paperclip springs up and hooks it, and a card asks if you forgot the file. Attach real files with the picker or by dropping them on the window, then the message folds into an envelope, the files slide in, a clip snaps on and it zooms away with a working Undo.
how: Write as usual; any mention of an attachment is underlined and the footer chip says You mention a file.
Press Send with nothing attached: the paperclip pops up, the words flash and a card offers Attach file or Send anyway.
Attach real files with the button or by dragging them onto the window; images show a thumbnail, others a type badge and size.
Send again: the body folds into an envelope, the files fly in, the flap shuts, a progress bar fills and it zooms off.
Undo within five seconds brings the whole draft and its files back.
